proofs: A preserved historical ID 47561749 above an unchanged local sequence does not block allocation of free IDs 2,3,4.
Existing records, frozen outbox, source hashes, receipts, admissions, quarantine and corporate contents remain unchanged.
The proof uses is_called, positive increment, no cycle, cache=1 and generator/int32 limits, not MAX(target_id) or historical row count.
The needed progression counts only waiting admissions without existing source mappings; no arbitrary range or offset is allocated.
Every prospective ID is checked against records in the bound namespace, global outbox IDs, local destination IDs and retained legacy receipts.
Immediate valid uniqueness constraints and visible ordinary tables are required; insufficient lock privileges refuse approval.
Per-transaction table locks exclude concurrent SQL writers, and immediate database uniqueness prevents duplicate local target IDs.
Each actual nextval value is checked independently of any prior forecast.
Conflicts in the requested interval block before materialization without consuming IDs; conflicts appearing after committed batches preserve those batches and block further work.
Never-called sequences use last_value itself as their first candidate.
Interruption, restart and repeated requests retain already committed IDs and do not create duplicate mappings.
MADM schema, full row comparisons, hashes, pause/recovery gates and selective quarantine are unchanged.
limits: Provided counts do not prove whether the production interval 2117158 through 2129427 is free; code must inspect the actual local occupancy.
Existing data does not certify the historical generator; all persisted IDs remain occupied independently of origin.
Unsupported cache, metadata, visibility, privileges, uniqueness or capacity keeps the block; no automatic sequence adjustment, skipping of occupied IDs or schema repair.
This is local allocation safety; the existing MADM collision checks and administrative release remain necessary.
Tests use smaller datasets and disposable PostgreSQL 16 with verified TLS; no production volume, query plans or latency were benchmarked.
